answer_text:
Given \(B(1)=1\), the increment from time \(1\) to time \(3\) is independent of the past and normally distributed:

\[
B(3)-B(1) \sim N(0,3-1)=N(0,2).
\]

Thus, conditional on \(B(1)=1\),

\[
B(3) = 1 + (B(3)-B(1)) \sim N(1,2).
\]

So

\[
P(B(3) \le 3 \mid B(1)=1)
= P\left(1+(B(3)-B(1)) \le 3\right).
\]

Let \(Z = \frac{B(3)-B(1)}{\sqrt{2}} \sim N(0,1)\). Then

\[
P(B(3) \le 3 \mid B(1)=1)
= P\left(Z \le \frac{3-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)
= \Phi\left(\sqrt{2}\right),
\]

where \(\Phi\) is the standard normal CDF.

\[
\boxed{\Phi(\sqrt{2})}
\]

27B·v4.method: Using independent increments of Brownian motion to reduce the conditional probability to a standard normal CDF evaluation.
